/bin/bash -lc "python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
p=Path('README.md');s=p.read_text()
s=s.replace('## Local setup and tests', '''## Unreleased Must increment: trusted Keeper/stream lifecycle

This working-tree increment is **not deployed**. The parent-verified "'`40bac966e410f1073d9a5bc1b0cb981315979970` foundation and [deployment handoff](docs/DEPLOYMENT.md) remain unchanged. Health still reports foundation/not-ready-for-raids. Raid Send Off, transfers/claims, lineage and automatic channel-ban synchronization remain separate pending work.

When OAuth is enabled, `createRuntime` now configures its actual memory/Firestore event store for the single configured streamer. Signed `stream.online`, `stream.offline` and chat commands pass through the same transaction as event dedupe, the **single global relic registry**, per-channel lifecycle state and mark context. The relic starts **unplaced**. Only initial home **raidrelichq `1591805230`**, after its own explicit opt-in and a verified current online stream, can originate it. Other opt-ins cannot take an existing holder. Offline or opt-out disables marking/display but does not release ownership to another opt-in. Incoming raid notifications continue to record the local ritual only; there is no ownership transfer path yet.

The signed broadcaster may say exactly **`!relic keep`** or **`!relic opt-in`**, and **`!relic opt-out`**. Neither viewers nor moderators can change consent/initial placement; text-supplied IDs/roles confer no authority. Opt-in before a verified online event records consent but leaves the relic unplaced until that event arrives. A paused, banned or safety-blocked channel cannot acquire. Pausing/resuming remains a signed broadcaster/moderator control. Existing private moderation, approved-rune projection, self-content-erasure, per-viewer five-mark quota and cross-stream 30-second cooldown remain enforced. Re-opting-in does not reset budgets or restore erased content.

**Session authority/order:** only the actual signed `stream.online.event.id` supplies a session ID, never dates or a command argument. Both subscription condition and event broadcaster must equal the configured channel, version 1, with valid online `type:live` and `started_at`. The HMAC/replay boundary still rejects stale/future transport timestamps. Stream lifecycle uses conservative signed timestamp watermarks and stream start times: old/duplicate online events cannot reset the current stream; offline wins a timestamp tie; an online start at/before an offline watermark, a closed ID, or an older stream start cannot reopen. Offline carries no trusted command-supplied stream ID; it closes the known session, clears its viewer counters and preserves cooldowns until their original expiry. New valid streams receive new budgets; late chat marks predating the current start/consent/offline boundary cannot spend them. This conservative policy can leave state waiting on ambiguous ordering rather than fabricate a session.

No stream snapshot is fetched at startup. If subscriptions are created after a stream is already online, this increment does **not** backfill an online event or invent its ID. It waits for the next genuine online event. Missed delivery, subscription revocation recovery, operator reconciliation with a trusted Helix stream snapshot and long-running liveness recovery are not implemented. Tests prove the stated ordering rules, not lossless EventSub delivery. A trustworthy initial-state recovery path remains a follow-up before broad live readiness.

The global `keeperRegistry` document contains only a single holder/origin flag and has a 4 KiB hard guard. Per-channel stream documents cap at 16 KiB, 16 closed stream IDs and 128 policy-blocked users. Store configuration allows at most four channel IDs for internal forward compatibility, but production runtime/OAuth still supplies **one** configured Keeper and validates exactly that streamer'"'s and bot's grants. It does not support a second logged-in channel or OlsOls2 yet. Marks retain the prior 128 KiB document/participant/content caps. At retention capacity, writes fail closed before dedupe commits; there is no silent reopening or quota discard. Actual multi-document atomicity is exercised using the staged Firestore fake, not a new live database test.

"'`runtime.state.setChannelPolicy(host, { banned, blockedUserIds })` is an internal trusted policy hook, with atomic context updates and public-feed notifications. No public policy endpoint exists; channel-ban syncing is still manual/pending. In lifecycle-enabled stores, `setKeeperContext` injection is disabled. Legacy explicit context injection remains only in standalone dev/test/simulator adapters, preserving existing fixtures without creating a production bypass.

### Subscription/bootstrap next step — explicit internal services

`runtime.subscriptions.payloads()` builds four version-1 webhook subscriptions for the configured channel: `stream.online`, `stream.offline`, incoming `channel.raid` (`to_broadcaster_user_id`) and `channel.chat.message` (streamer + bot IDs). It makes no HTTP call. `runtime.subscriptions.setup()` / `.reconcile()` are explicit privileged service calls: they validate the stored streamer/bot token identities and grants, obtain an app token, list subscriptions (at most five 100-item pages), retain matching enabled/pending subscriptions, and create only missing ones. Pagination loops/capacity, API failures and conflicts stop safely. They do not delete subscriptions, run periodically, execute at startup, or have an unauthenticated admin route. API responses/logs never include tokens or the webhook secret.

Official [stream online/offline and raid subscription documentation](https://dev.twitch.tv/docs/eventsub/eventsub-subscription-types/) confirms these types require no additional user authorization scopes; webhook creation still uses an app access token. Chat retains bot `user:read:chat`/`user:bot` plus broadcaster `channel:bot` (rather than assuming moderation); bot `user:write:chat` is for sending, and the already-committed streamer `channel:manage:raids` is for future Send Off, not lifecycle receipt. No scopes were added. See [EventSub management](https://dev.twitch.tv/docs/eventsub/manage-subscriptions/) and existing token identity checks. Only public docs were read; all HTTP tests are mocks.

**Bootstrap is not complete:** after an authorized future release, the owner must explicitly connect the configured streamer/bot grants. A parent-operated, authenticated internal harness/operator integration must then invoke subscription setup/reconcile. That operational harness/UI is not supplied as a public endpoint and was not run here. Until the chat subscription exists, `!relic keep` cannot bootstrap its own delivery. Once setup and genuine online delivery are established, the broadcaster'"'s own chat command reliably initializes the home relic via the wired transaction; no privileged context injection is needed. A stream already in progress at setup still needs the trusted initial-state recovery described above or a subsequent genuine online event. No OAuth login, subscription creation, chat message, raid, cloud operation or deployment was performed by Codex.

## Local setup and tests''',1)

Implemented trusted lifecycle routing with atomic event dedupe, a single relic-holder registry, signed stream IDs, and broadcaster-only opt-in/opt-out. Only raidrelichq can originate the unplaced relic; other opt-ins cannot take it.

Added explicit internal subscription setup/reconcile services, ordering protections, and regression tests preserving quotas and content erasure.

**119 tests: 115 pass, 4 sandbox socket skips, 0 failures.**

Bootstrap still needs operator subscription setup; already-online stream backfill remains pending. Send Off/transfers are deferred. README/AGENTS updated. Deployed `40bac…` foundation unchanged; no commits, cloud/live calls, or credential reads.
